Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

- Adult male (34 y) with subacute fatigue and migratory arthralgia preceded by self-resolving annular calf rash after hiking in the U.S.  
- Most likely etiology: early disseminated Lyme disease; alternative considerations include post-viral fatigue (EBV/CMV) and hypothyroidism.  
- No red-flag symptoms (weight loss, night sweats, focal neuro deficits).  
- Working diagnosis: probable Lyme disease – pending serology.  
- Plan: order blood tests (CBC, U&E, LFT, TSH, inflammatory markers, Lyme serology +/- viral serology). Phone follow-up 1 week after results. Consider doxycycline course if Lyme serology positive or clinically indicated.  

Management Plan

- Pathology form issued for above tests.  
- Arrange virtual review 1 week post-testing.  
- Educated patient on possible Lyme disease, indications for antibiotics, and to seek care sooner if worsening symptoms (fever, joint swelling, new neuro/cardiac symptoms).  
- Encourage gradual return to physical activity as tolerated; maintain balanced diet.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):

1. Lyme disease (High) – timeline of outdoor exposure, annular rash, subsequent fatigue/arthralgia strongly suggestive.  
2. Post-viral fatigue/EBV-CMV (Moderate) – preceding sore throat/low-grade fever and prolonged fatigue could fit chronic viral course.  
3. Hypothyroidism (Moderate) – common cause of fatigue/myalgias; to be screened with TSH.
